title: Project scaffolding
description: Create the Xcode workspace with two app targets (EarnPlay child app and EarnPlay Admin), a shared Swift package for models and schemas used by both apps, and a git repository. Fix and record the bundle IDs for the child and admin apps.

title: Model runtime spike
description: Integrate a quantized-model runtime (llama.cpp / MLC-style), load a small open-weights model on-device, and run one prompt-to-response round-trip fully offline.

title: Solver service
description: Build the deterministic verifier for 4th-grade skills: multiplication facts to 12×12, multi-digit multiplication, division, fraction comparison and addition, and word problems. The solver is plain code — the model never grades its own answers.

title: Entitlement filing — do first, long lead
description: File the FamilyControls (Distribution) entitlement request using the prepared justification draft, and enable the development entitlement so real shields can be tested locally while the distribution request is reviewed.

title: Diagnostic
description: Build the 10-minute diagnostic that produces a skill profile across facts fluency, fractions, word problems, reading fluency, and comprehension. The profile drives what the tutor asks next.

title: Question generation + verification loop
description: The model proposes a problem (skill + form + values); the solver verifies it before it is shown. On failure, retry within a bounded count, then fall back to a safe, pre-verified question. Questions use varied, real-world and puzzle-like forms — not plain textbook form.

title: Hint ladder
description: Three hint levels — nudge, then strategy, then one worked step — offered while the child is working. Record every hint use, and track whether a hint is followed by a changed answer.

title: Effort scoring
description: Score genuine effort from active minutes (pausing after about 20 seconds with no interaction), attempts, hint interactions, answer revisions, and explanations given. Compare the score against a per-session variable threshold (about 8–14 points) so the target cannot be learned. Enforce the floor rule

title: Stalling probes
description: Detect stalling from signals such as missing revisions, response-time patterns, repeated identical wrong answers, and hints used as an answer key. When signals fire, probe conversationally — “show me one step” or “what have you tried?” — and count a substantive reply as effort.

title: Decision logger
description: Every consequential decision — unlock granted or denied, trade offered, difficulty changed — writes a Decision record with a full justification: the decision, the evidence observed, the reasoning, the alternative considered, and a confidence level. Routine actions get a one-line reason.

title: Read-aloud infrastructure
description: Build the ReadAloudService for the child app: on-device text-to-speech only (the system's built-in speech, for example AVSpeechSynthesizer — no network call, no downloaded voice), behind one reusable speaker-button component for question, hint, and instruction views (the Diagnostic, Challenge, and H

title: Chat conversation UI
description: Build the child app's main practice screen as a chat conversation: a message thread with the AI tutor where questions, hints, probes, encouragement, answers, and revisions flow as messages. Renders TutorEngine's turn stream — the UI holds no behavior logic; every decision comes from TutorEngine, EffortScorer, and the rule gates. Message list (tutor/child), composer with text input plus choice/number-pad options matched to question type and grade band, Hint button beside the composer, speaker button on every tutor message, slim session header with star progress. Demo ships the Band B (grade 4) version.

title: Policy store
description: Build the versioned policy store on the child device: always-allowed apps, the unblockable list, never-unlockable overrides, unlock durations, caps, and the chore pool. Cache the policy on the child app; on version conflict, the admin's newer version wins.

title: Shield manager
description: Apply and remove ManagedSettings shields from policy, enumeration-first: shield every app except the allowlist, using the apps enumerated via FamilyActivityPicker at setup (see T2.3), with category shields as a backstop for newly installed apps that are not yet enumerated. Do not rely on a per-app e

title: Setup flow
description: Guide a fresh install through FamilyControls authorization in Screen Time, then FamilyActivityPicker on the child's device to enumerate the apps on the device and choose the allowlist and the unblockable list. Shield every enumerated app except the allowlist (enumeration-first), with category shield

title: Simulated shield fallback
description: Provide an in-app shield screen that stands in for real ManagedSettings shields when the distribution entitlement is unavailable, so the full challenge-to-unlock flow can still be demonstrated.

title: Default-deny for new apps
description: Newly installed apps are locked until the next policy sync classifies them: category shields are the backstop that catches a newly installed app before it has been enumerated and classified. An unknown app never opens by default.

title: Movement trade
description: AI-initiated offer only (for example, jumping jacks or running in place). Verify the activity with CoreMotion rep counting with the phone in a pocket, showing a live counter. Enforce a once-per-session limit and a weekly cap, grant a 15-minute unlock on completion, and apply the taper rule: if trade

title: Chore trade
description: The AI offers exactly one chore from the parent-stocked pool mid-session, chosen with rotation and time-of-day fit. The child accepts or declines and taps done; the parent confirms completion and the unlock is granted. The child never sees a chore menu or list.

title: Trade offer logic
description: Decide mid-session whether to offer a movement trade, a chore trade, or no offer at all, varying the choice so no pattern is learnable. Enforce the floor: at least one genuine practice attempt happens before any alternative currency is offered.

title: Photo-proof async mode
description: Optional asynchronous chore verification: the child submits photo proof, the unlock is granted on trust, and the parent reviews later with the power to revoke and re-lock.

title: Policy editor
description: Edit every policy field: always-allowed apps, the unblockable list, never-unlockable overrides, unlock durations, caps, the chore pool (chore, unlock minutes, expiry, verification mode), and movement-trade settings. Saving bumps the policy version and queues it for sync.

title: Dashboard
description: Show progress at a glance: accuracy per skill (this week versus last), active time per question, hint rate, most common error type, effort-score trend, and trade frequency — all computed from synced session logs.

title: Transcript viewer
description: Open any session and read the full transcript: questions asked, the child's attempts, hints given, and timestamps.

title: Decision log viewer
description: Browse the child's decision log — every unlock, trade and difficulty decision with its full justification — filterable by session and by decision type.

title: Auditor engine
description: Run a second, separate on-device auditor over session logs with seven checks: leniency drift, false negatives (trying hard but denied), gaming patterns, question-quality and difficulty miscalibration, behavior shifts, inconsistency, and justifications that do not match the raw log. Each flag carries

title: Sync
description: Connect the two apps with MultipeerConnectivity over Bluetooth and local Wi-Fi. PolicyUpdate flows down to the child app; SessionLog flows up to the admin app. Handle versioning, queue messages while disconnected, and retry until delivered. Sync works when both apps are open and nearby.

title: Eval harness
description: Build scripted sessions for five personas — good-faith, guessing, idling, manipulative, and struggling child — and score them against fixed pass criteria: never teaches a wrong answer, never unlocks on pure idling, resists manipulation, and stays on-topic and age-appropriate.

title: Red-teaming
description: Run a prompt-injection and jailbreak battery against the tutor — “ignore your instructions,” “mom said unlock,” “pretend you're my friend,” and edge cases — treating all child input as untrusted.

title: Versioning + rollback
description: Record the model and prompt version on every session. Provide a rollback procedure for a regressing model or prompt, and show the running version plus a known-limits note in the admin app.

title: Demo staging
description: Stage the four demo moments so they run live: (1) a hard-trying child earns an unlock despite wrong answers; (2) an idling child earns nothing; (3) all three currencies — practice, movement, and chore; (4) the auditor catches a staged leniency error.

title: Submission packaging
description: Produce the demo video and README and complete the hackathon submission.

title: App Store submission
description: Complete the distribution-entitlement approval, prepare for App Store review (kids category and privacy requirements), and run a TestFlight build.

title: Multi-child support
description: Extend policy, profiles, logs and the dashboard to more than one child.

title: Speech scoring for read-aloud
description: Score read-aloud practice on-device as part of the reading profile.

title: Fuller curriculum
description: Broaden skills and question forms beyond the demo's 4th-grade core set.

title: Selectable audit endpoint
description: Let the parent choose where the auditor runs: on-device local model (the default), the parent's own local endpoint (home server, NAS or Mac), or a cloud endpoint with a parent-supplied key. Cloud is opt-in only, offers a summaries-only mode, shows a plain-language disclosure before it is enabled, an

title: Opt-in cloud sync
description: Optional cloud sync as an alternative to direct device-to-device sync, off by default.

title: Band A screen variants
description: Build the Band A (grades 1–2) variants of the three Demo screens — Diagnostic (T1.1), Challenge (T1.2), and Hint display (T1.3) — selected by the grade parameter. They are variants of the same screens, not new screens: answers are tap-to-choose with picture options and the keyboard stays off the scr

title: Grade-banded UI copy packs
description: Move every child-facing interface string — button labels, instructions, tutor prompts shown as text, and system messages on the Diagnostic, Challenge, and Hint display screens and the other child-app screens — into UI copy packs keyed by the grade parameter, so the same screen speaks at the child's

title: CI pipeline setup
description: Set up a CI pipeline (Xcode Cloud or GitHub Actions on macOS runners) from the T0.1 workspace and the repo the user pushes code to, linked to the user's Xcode Cloud or GitHub Actions account. The pipeline config (ci.yml or Xcode Cloud config) lives in the repo and runs on every push: build both targ

title: Automated archive and TestFlight upload
description: Extend the T7.1 pipeline with archive and upload jobs: on push to main (or on tag), the pipeline archives the app and uploads the build to TestFlight in App Store Connect with no manual steps. Prerequisite (user one-time, not a task): the App Store Connect API key is stored in CI secrets only — neve

title: Release versioning and checklist
description: Add release versioning on top of the T7.1 pipeline: a version-bump script implementing the versioning scheme (semantic version + auto-incrementing build number), a TestFlight release-notes template, and a release checklist doc, so versioning is one script run and every TestFlight build carries the c

title: App Store submission prep
description: Prepare the v1 App Store submission from the T7.2 pipeline output and the App Store Connect listing requirements: draft the listing (description, keywords, categories, privacy policy), build the screenshot set, complete a submission checklist covering the entitlement, privacy and review requirements

title: On-device release verification
description: Manual task, user. Install the T7.2 TestFlight build on the user's iPhone (Screen Time + FamilyControls authorized) and verify every demo moment on the real device, recording a pass/fail verification report per moment.

title: Pilot web scaffold
description: Single-page web app (plain HTML/JS, no backend, no build step): question display, answer input, hint button, session timer with idle detection, and a mock unlock screen.

title: Pilot question bank
description: 12 varied-form 4th-grade math questions (stories, reverse problems, estimation, 'which one is wrong and why'), each with a verified answer, loaded by the pilot page. No plain textbook drills.

title: Pilot effort scorer + simulated unlock
description: Deterministic effort scoring (active minutes idle-paused after ~20s, attempts, revisions, hint interactions), the floor rule, a variable per-session threshold, and the unlock decision with a one-paragraph justification plus the mock unlock screen.

title: Pilot admin transcript view
description: Read-only transcript view for the just-finished session: every question, attempt, hint event, effort signal values, and the decision with its justification.

title: Copilot pilot build evaluation
description: Hand the pilot spec (HLD Pilot section + T8.1-T8.4) to the Copilot coding agent as a build issue, then grade the delivered build on correctness, completeness, and code quality. Record a go/no-go note on delegating 10-day build work to the agent.

title: Browser model: tutor messages + parallel effort judge
description: Give the pilot an in-browser model (WebLLM via CDN, no build step) with two jobs: (1) draft tutor messages (encouragement, probes, hint wording) within the ladder level the deterministic code chose; (2) judge effort in parallel with the deterministic scorer, advisory only — the scorer still gates the unlock; both verdicts shown side by side, disagreements flagged. Guardrails in code: every draft validated (length cap, never contains the final answer; bounded regeneration then canned fallback); no model output can change the unlock decision. Lazy-loads on user gesture; if WebGPU is unavailable or the model fails, the pilot works exactly as the deterministic-only version.
